title: Fastpath control-plane stall: on-call checklist and immediate playbook
linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE: Private VPC runbook v2 (doc id 8742)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a concise on-call checklist and quick playbook for when the control-plane path used for fastpath/agent heartbeats stalls or shows intermittent reachability problems in private/VPC and on-prem customers. Focus is on first 30–90 minutes: restore reachability, mitigate impact, and gather artifacts for a follow-up postmortem. Not a final runbook — working draft for pager responders.

Short summary (problem pattern):
- Symptoms: control plane heartbeat ACKs drop, agent reconnects fail, customer control-plane metrics show increased RTT and spikes in connection resets.
- Typical downstream impact: tenant control-plane operations (policy push, agent check-ins) delayed or failed; traffic dataplane generally continues but policy changes stall.
- Common correlates from past incidents: conntrack exhaustion, MTU fragmentation during policy rollout, DNAT/SNAT shadowing from customer FW, BGP flapping on the customer edge, or control-plane proxy thread exhaustion.

Detection & quick triage (first 5 min):
1) Confirm alerts: check PagerDuty ticket, slack #oncall-private, and alerts dashboard (ControlPlane/HeartbeatErrorRate, Agent-Reconnects). Note start time.
2) Determine scope: single tenant vs multi-tenant vs entire region. Quick query in Observability:
   - Query: controlplane.heartbeat.failures grouped by tenant (last 15m)
   - If single tenant -> suspect customer-side FW/NAT; if many tenants -> suspect internal fabric or control-plane proxy layer.
3) Check control-plane pod health: kubectl -n controlplane get pods -o wide; describe the primary control-plane pods.
4) Run basic connectivity checks from control-plane to a problematic agent (pick a failing agent node IP):
   - curl -v http://<agent-ip>:<health-port>/healthz
   - nc -vz <agent-ip> <control-plane-port>
   - From control-plane host: ping, traceroute to agent IP.
5) Check recent deploys/rollouts: git/CI activity in last 30m (Circle/GitHub Actions), and any infra autoscale events.

Immediate mitigations (first 15–30 min):
A) If symptoms point to conntrack exhaustion on customer gateway (single tenant):
   - Confirm conntrack table size: ssh to the edge/agent host (if accessible) and run: sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count; sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
   - Temporarily increase nf_conntrack_max (short-term): sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 (record change and plan rollback)
   - Clear conntrack entries for the control-plane port only: sudo conntrack -D -p tcp --dport <control-plane-port> --orig-src <agent-ip> (avoid full flush unless agreed).
B) If symptoms point to MTU fragmentation (packet drops during large policy push):
   - Check path MTU: sudo tracepath <agent-ip> or ping -s <size> -M do <agent-ip>.
   - If fragmentation evident, temporarily reduce policy bundle size or switch to incremental policies. Halt any ongoing full-rollout.
C) If customer firewall DNAT/SNAT shadowing suspected (we see mismatched src/dst in logs):
   - Engage oncall SE / customer contact (use contact card in ticket). Request a quick firewall translation table dump if allowed.
   - If control-plane proxy supports alternate egress, trigger fallback route: route control-plane traffic via alternate NAT gateway or relay (config op: set controlplane.egress.override=<relay-host>), or shift to TCP keepalive tuning.
D) If multi-tenant spike / internal proxy overload:
   - Scale control-plane proxy pool (k8s HPA or manual instance add). Run: kubectl scale deployment/controlplane-proxy --replicas=<N+2>.
   - Enable circuit-breaker to route new connections to less loaded region (if configured).

Artifact collection (essential for post-incident):
- control-plane logs (last 30m) for controlplane-*.log from affected pods and nodes (collect with log scraper).
- tcpdump capture on control-plane and affected agent host: sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/cp-agent-<ts>.pcap host <agent-ip> and port <control-plane-port>. Capture 60s.
- conntrack list snapshot: sudo conntrack -L > /tmp/conntrack-<ts>.txt
- netstat/tcp states: ss -tn src <control-plane-ip> or ss -tn state CLOSE-WAIT | wc -l
- Output of sysctl net.* and iptables -t nat -S on edge nodes.
- Observability graphs and alert timestamps: link as screenshot or saved graph.

Runbook steps (ordered procedure for oncall):
1) Acknowledge the pager and create/annotate a dedicated incident ticket. Add oncall responder names and initial hypothesis in the ticket.
2) Confirm scope (see Detection). If single-customer, spin up private coordination channel with SE + customer.
3) Stabilize traffic: if a rollout is in-progress, pause it. If policy pushes are queued, suspend or throttle bulk pushes.
4) Execute targeted conntrack remediation (see A). Do NOT full-flush conntrack unless a mitigation TTL is approved.
5) If scaling is required, scale control-plane proxies first (see D). Monitor latency and error rate for 5 min.
6) If fallback/re-route is available, fail traffic to relay and monitor for recovery.
7) If no improvement after 20–30 min, escalate to on-call infra lead and open a wider war-room.

Useful commands (oncall cheat-sheet):
- Check control-plane errors: kubectl -n controlplane logs deployment/controlplane --since=30m | grep -i error
- Pod-level network debug: kubectl exec -n controlplane <pod> -- /bin/sh -c "tcpdump -n -i any port <control-plane-port> -c 200 -w /tmp/capture.pcap"
- Conntrack inspect: sudo conntrack -L | grep <agent-ip> | tail -n 100
- Clear conntrack for a flow: sudo conntrack -D -p tcp --orig-src <agent-ip> --dport <control-plane-port>
- MTU check: tracepath <agent-ip> or ping -M do -s 1472 <agent-ip>
- Check iptables DNAT rules: sudo iptables -t nat -S | grep -i <control-plane-port>

Customer comms (recommended fast message template):
- Short message to SE on-call: "We observed control-plane heartbeat failures for your tenant around <time>. We're investigating. Short-term action: temporarily increased conntrack table and paused policy rollouts. We'll update in 20 minutes or when traffic normalizes. Need your firewall translation table or permission to run targeted conntrack clear on your gateway?"

Follow-ups and post-incident actions (owner assignment during incident):
- Collect all artifacts and link them in the incident ticket.
- If conntrack exhaustion was root cause: create action to tune conntrack defaults for affected deployment profiles and add conntrack monitoring and alerting for per-tenant thresholds.
- If MTU/policy size contributed: add a preflight check for policy bundle size that validates path MTU and fallback to segmented push.
- If firewall DNAT shadowing found: write a short KB for SEs with standard firewall table checks and a sample conntrack clear command.
- Schedule a follow-up postmortem within 3 business days; assign RCA owner.

Open questions / research items (notes to self):
- Can we add a control-plane synthetic heartbeat from multiple vantage points (internal relay + direct) to differentiate NAT translations vs internal route faults?
- Should we offer a per-tenant conntrack headroom metric in Console/Optimize for onprem customers?
- Investigate whether control-plane proxy should proactively adjust keepalive and TCP window tuning for customers behind aggressive firewalls.

References and quick links:
- Internal runbooks: CONFLUENCE: Private VPC runbook v2 (doc id 8742)
- Jira: JIRA-PI-4521 (incident intake)
- Infra PR for conntrack tuning (draft): github.com/redwood-inference/rw-infra/pull/789

Notes (working log):
- 2026-08-15 09:12 PDT — Pager triggered, single-tenant, spike in heartbeat error rate. Added Ravi and Olga.
- 2026-08-15 09:19 PDT — Confirmed conntrack count at ~120k / max 131072 on edge; cleared candidate flows for control-plane port and saw partial recovery.
- 2026-08-15 09:33 PDT — Paused policy rollout; control-plane latencies back to baseline after targeted conntrack clears.
- Keep accurate timestamps for final postmortem.

This doc is intentionally terse and designed for rapid consumption during a pager. Add improvements and edge-case checks as we iterate. If you used or changed any host-level knobs (sysctl, conntrack flush), record the exact commands and reason in the incident ticket for audit and rollback.
